newsitem.title: INDIA: Congress party says it may review Indian budget.
newsitem.headline: Congress party says it may review Indian budget.

text.p: India's Congress party said on Sunday it might amend some of the budget proposals of Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's government in case the Congress succeeded in its bid to head a new coalition.
Congress general secretary Ghulam Nabi Azad told Reuters: "We will see what changes are needed and implement them."

Former finance minister Manmohan Singh, a senior Congress leader, told Reuters a change in the government would not cause any crisis in the federal budget for fiscal 1997/98 (April-March) presented in parliament on February 28.
"The vote on account has been passed. So we have four months to go before a budget becomes due," Singh said.
A vote on account is a temporary measure that authorises the government to borrow money from the treasury to meet its expenses. The budget has not yet been approved by parliament.
Singh said a change in government would not deter foreign investors, adding: "They know there is a broad political consensus for economic reforms in India which cannot be altered."
